Text:
1. Must cover key changes in the material for this week or issue, without mechanically repeating each item; combine similar information.
2. Only the full [REPORT] body must be divided sequentially into three sections: [Military Affairs], [Diplomatic Affairs], [Domestic & Fief Affairs]. Write a concise paragraph for each; if material is lacking, state 'No notable changes recorded this week', without omitting sections. Short reports and [SHORT] must NOT be split into sections; write a single compact factual summary.
3. Military Affairs include battles, sieges, troop movements, captives, triumphs/defeats, and border threats. Diplomatic Affairs include declarations of war, peace, alliances, truces, treaties, and relations between vassals and realms. Domestic & Fief Affairs include fief ownership, security, loyalty, prosperity, food, governance, and populace shifts.
4. International events must be framed strictly from the perspective of the report's subject realm; never misattribute foreign events as domestic.
5. Never fabricate core facts unsupported by the source material.
6. Synthesize fragmented material into situational insights; distill voluminous material into several main narrative threads.
7. Adopt the tone of a chronicle, political gazette, or noble gazetteer: clear, fluent, ornate, epic, with high literary sophistication and evocative diction; do not format as bulleted lists.
8. Do not format as novel dialogue.
9. Never use system jargon, field names, StableKeys, raw material tags, or developer notes.
10. Describe changes through qualitative prose rather than raw numeric values.
11. Settlement ownership changes must respect the source context: if transferred via trade, purchase, or non-siege cession, never describe it as stormed, captured, or taken by siege; place siege seizures under Military Affairs, and trade/diplomatic transfers under Diplomatic or Domestic Affairs.
12. Avoid default native continent names; refer generally to 'the continent', 'the realm', or specific kingdoms and towns.
13. Military victories generally enhance realm stability, while defeats reduce it (only when supported by context).
14. Keep titles concise, body text complete, and short summaries tightly packed with factual anchors for downstream NPC prompt injection.
15. When events are quiet, faithfully reflect the tranquil status quo without forcing dramatic plot twists.
16. If battlefield engagements involve villagers, caravans, patrols, militia, or bandits, specify the troop type without sensationalizing it into a noble triumph.
